Regional Vice President of Operations
May River Recruiting
Tulsa, OK
We are partnering with a private-equity-backed residential and light-commercial services platform. They operate local HVAC, plumbing and electrical brands across the South and Southeast. The brands keep their local names and the customer relationships they've built over decades. The platform brings the playbooks, systems, pricing, talent and capital to make every branch perform like our best one.
THE OPPORTUNITY
We're looking for an operator to run one of our regions as its owner. You'll own the P&L for a $100M+ region and every number that builds it — revenue, gross margin, labor, materials, EBITDA and the cash behind them — across six to nine branches, and you'll lead the General Managers who run them.
This isn't a liaison or coaching seat. Our platform leaders build the standards for sales, operations, pricing and inventory. You're accountable for the results those standards are built to produce, branch by branch. You'll find problems before anyone asks, show up with the fix, and hold the standard with every GM — including founders and long-tenured leaders who built these businesses.
If you've run a multi-site service business, built GMs who win without you in the room, and want a seat where results are yours and the pay follows them, we want to talk.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
Results
Regional and branch P&L: Revenue, gross margin, labor, materials, SG&A and EBITDA against budget for the region and every branch in it.
Cash flow: Revenue isn't done until it's collected. You own accounts receivable, aging, collections and billing speed in every branch, and you work AR weekly, not at quarter-end.
Growth: Organic growth in every branch through memberships, technician-generated leads, unsold-estimate follow-up and new service lines.
Forecasts you deliver: Quarterly and full-year commitments you make and then hit.
The drivers behind them
Labor and productivity: Hours, overtime, headcount and technician productivity managed weekly and in season.
Materials and inventory: Job costing, truck stock and warehouse controls.
Sales-cycle execution: Close rate, options presented and average ticket moving toward top quartile in every branch.
Pricing discipline: Pricebook and discount standards followed every time.
Customer experience: Booking speed, maintenance renewals, online reputation and customer sentiment.
Your people
GM bench: A strong GM in every seat and a ready successor for every branch.
Retention and safety: Teams that stay, and branches that run safely and in compliance.
HOW YOU'LL RUN THE REGION
Daily: Labor, hours, materials and open customer issues — caught the same day, not at month-end.
Weekly: Branch scorecards with each GM, labor sign-off before payroll, AR aging and collections review, and a written regional update to the COO.
In the field: Tuesday through Thursday in branches — GM working sessions, ride-alongs, call center and warehouse time. Every branch visited on a set rotation.
Monthly: A P&L review for every branch with Finance, and a recovery plan for every miss.
Quarterly: Regional business review, talent and succession review, and an updated full-year forecast.

Own regional and branch financial results, and move resources across branches to protect the region.
Hire, develop, evaluate and, when needed, replace General Managers.
Teach GMs to diagnose their own business: which number is off, why, and what they're changing this week.
Get our operating standards running in every branch and measure adoption weekly.
Lead branch turnarounds and regional growth initiatives.
Integrate acquired businesses onto our systems and standards, and help founder-led teams make the transition.
Partner with platform leaders in sales, operations, pricing, finance, marketing and HR.
Present regional performance to executive leadership and the board.
Build one team across your branches and the home office.

Multi-unit leadership: You've led five or more site or branch leaders at once, with results that held after you moved on.

Sr. Manufacturing Process Engineer, Robotics
Tesla
Austin, TX
What To Expect
The Sr. Manufacturing Process Engineer, Robotics, leads process design and industrialization efforts that deliver exceptional product quality and volumes for next-generation electric motors manufacturing. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams—including design engineering, die engineering, tooling suppliers, quality, automation, and operations—to improve throughput, reduce scrap and downtime, and ensure processes meet Tesla’s rigorous standards for performance, safety, and sustainability. This position blends advanced stamping expertise, materials science for electrical steels, tooling/process optimization, automation integration, and data-driven continuous improvement in a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment.
What You'll Do
Develop, qualify, and optimize high-speed stamping processes (progressive, compound, or hybrid dies) for electric motor laminations from electrical steel coil, ensuring precise geometry, flatness, edge quality, and coating integrity to maximize motor efficiency and minimize core losses
Specify, design/review, validate, and industrialize dies, tooling, press parameters, lubrication, strip feeding, and material handling systems tailored to electrical steels (silicon steels and advanced grades)
Integrate and optimize automation elements—including robotics, PLCs, sensors, vision systems, servo/VFD controls, and end-of-line stacking/bonding equipment—to achieve high throughput, consistent quality inspection, and automated lamination stacking or interlocking
Troubleshoot process, tooling, press, and automation issues on the production floor; lead root-cause analysis (RCA) and implement permanent corrective actions to minimize downtime and scrap
Partner with product design, die engineering, tooling suppliers, quality, and maintenance teams on Design for Manufacturability (DFM), Design for Assembly (DFA), equipment validation (IQ/OQ/PQ), process capability (Cpk), and industrialization of new motor designs and production lines
Drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and advanced methods—such as predictive maintenance, energy-efficient press operation, scrap reduction/recycling of electrical steel, and waste minimization—aligned with Tesla’s sustainability goals
Support new product introduction (NPI) and production ramp-up by transferring processes into manufacturing, training operators/technicians, and ensuring robust, scalable workflows
Ensure full compliance with safety standards (including safety PLCs and fail-safe systems), quality systems, regulatory requirements, and environmental goals throughout process and equipment lifecycle
What You'll Bring
Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or equivalent experience
5+ years of experience in manufacturing process engineering within high-volume production environments, preferably automotive, electric motors, precision metal stamping, or electrical steel/component manufacturing. Senior-level ownership of process development and industrialization is expected

Demonstrated ability to perform data analysis, statistical process control, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma (Green/Black Belt preferred), DOE, and tools such as Minitab or equivalent
Knowledge of secondary lamination processes (stacking, interlocking, bonding, welding) and quality metrology (dimensional, optical, coating, and ideally magnetic property evaluation) is highly desirable
Excellent problem-solving skills with a hands-on approach to debugging complex process and equipment issues in a production setting
Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with occasional overtime or shift work to support 24/7 manufacturing
Travel as required for equipment/die supplier visits, trials or buyoffs (>5%)

Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
